construct: ATP7A encodes a P-type copper-transporting ATPase that transports copper across cellular membranes and is essential for intestinal copper absorption and tissue copper distribution. Severe ATP7A loss of function produces systemic copper deficiency and reduced activity of multiple copper-dependent enzymes.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Male infant with early neurodegeneration, kinky lightly pigmented hair, low copper/ceruloplasmin, and ATP7A loss has Menkes disease from impaired ATP-dependent copper transport.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Wilson disease is the closest copper-transport alternative, but ATP7B loss causes impaired biliary excretion and copper accumulation, whereas ATP7A loss produces impaired absorption/distribution with low copper and classic kinky-hair neurodegeneration. Iron, heme, and cystine transport defects are mechanistically distinct.
